title: Prizes & Settlement
subtitle: Prize money by position and share, and ticket payouts
summary: Prizes & Settlement turns a certified result into money: prize schedules from the purse, awards split to owners by their ownership share on race day plus trainer and jockey percentages, approval and payment, and payouts of winning tickets with tax withholding for large wins.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The purse is split by finishing position using the PRIZE_SPLIT_1..5 settings. Each placed horse's share is divided again: TRAINER_SHARE_PCT to the trainer, JOCKEY_SHARE_PCT to the jockey, and the rest to the owners in proportion to the shares they held on race day, asked live from the Horse Registry.
Positions with no runner return their money to the purse (PRIZE_UNAWARDED). Awards go through approval before payment, so a second person checks the numbers.
Winning tickets are loaded from Wagering. Above the withholding threshold the winner must be identified and tax is withheld before the payout can be approved.

sections.title: Prizes & Settlement database architecture · Visual ERD
sections.intro: Your MySQL prizes_settlement schema contains three tables and five foreign keys. The diagram distinguishes race prize awards from winning wager-ticket payouts and shows their dependencies on Race Operations, Wagering and shared party master data.

sections.title: First, understand the two ways money is paid out
paragraphs: Prize awards: A horse finishes in a prize-paying position. The club knows the amount for that position from prize_schedule. The backend then determines which people or organisations should receive an award—owners, jockeys, trainers or others—and records their individual prize_award entries.

Winning-ticket payouts: Separately, a bettor presents a winning ticket. That transaction begins in Wagering, while ticket_payout records the payout amount, any tax withheld, payment status and payment reference.

These are not the same obligation. A winning horse receives a prize distribution; a winning betting ticket receives a dividend payout. Both involve money leaving the club, but they have different source records, beneficiaries and business rules.

sections.title: What MySQL guarantees — and what the service must guarantee
items: SQL checks: prize amounts cannot be negative; for awards, net must equal gross minus withholding; ticket paid amount must equal gross minus tax withheld.
SQL uniqueness: one prize schedule per race and finishing position; one ticket_payout per ticket; payment reference is unique when provided (MySQL unique indexes can allow multiple NULLs).
SQL references: awards must reference an existing race result and beneficiary party; payouts reference an existing wager ticket and may reference a beneficiary.

Business logic: verify certified results, race-day ownership history, trainer/jockey sharing rules, eligible winning tickets, tax rules, approvals and authorized disbursements. None of those algorithms are fully expressed in this DDL.
Financial integrity: avoid duplicate payments and duplicate GL postings. Account for withholding liabilities and reconcile actual cash movement. A foreign key alone cannot ensure a transfer occurred.

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Prize money uses ownership on race day, not today: history from the registry pays the right people.
Paying a ticket here marks it PAID in Wagering through its API, so the two modules can never disagree.
